reason: Reproduced end to end at 1440x960 against the real source (render-b.js), not the frames. Opened row 4 ("Choose the evening music"), pressed the -7 step, then "Delete this moment". All three distinct claims hold and none is covered by interaction-check.mjs, which only asserts that delete removes the moment and that the measure reflows (lines 530-533). (1) document.activeElement is BODY immediately after the delete, and stays BODY through the subsequent Undo press: the delete branch (render-b.js:503-509) calls closeEditor(root, false) - the false path skips the return-focus - then item.remove(), and nothing takes focus after. closeEditor's own focus contract is proven for Escape (gate line 487) but is deliberately bypassed here, and the row that held focus no longer exists, so there is no fallback. (2) Announcement: at rest there is one role=status node (.b-undo); with the editor open there are two (.b-stepRead role=status is the second). After the delete the stepRead node is gone with the panel and .b-undo's textContent is byte-identical to what it was before the delete. A live region whose text does not change fires nothing, so a screen-reader owner is told nothing about the single destructive act on the surface. That is the exact inverse of the comment at render-b.js:270-272, which reasons carefully about not announcing a change that did not happen while leaving a change that did happen silent. (3) The bar keeps reading "Last change: Choose the evening music moved 7 days closer." with data-empty="false" and .b-undoAct enabled - a live offer to restore a row that has been destroyed. Pressing it runs undo() (render-b.js:481): history.pop() succeeds, querySelector('.b-item[data-id="demo-audience-item-music"]') returns null, the if (item) block is skipped, and paintUndo repaints the bar empty. Row count stays at 6, the moment is not restored, focus stays on BODY, and the record of the move is destroyed too. So the surface's one reversibility affordance both fails to cover the one irreversible action and makes a false claim in its place. Real, specific, not taste, breaks no constraint, and fixing it is a small build.
sharpenedFix: The fix is right in shape but wrong in one mechanism and loose in two places. (a) Do NOT serialise the row to outerHTML. item.remove() detaches the node without destroying it, so keep the live node reference: var next = item.nextElementSibling; item.remove(); history.push({ kind: 'delete', node: item, title: record.title, measure: measureEl, nextNode: next }). An outerHTML round-trip re-parses to a fresh element and drops anything not expressed in markup (any property, listener, or measured state place() or setAway may have set), and it is a needless serialisation of a node you already hold. Restoring is then measureEl.insertBefore(last.node, last.nextNode && last.nextNode.isConnected ? last.nextNode : null) - the isConnected guard matters because the recorded neighbour can itself have been deleted since, which a stored data-id lookup would silently mishandle. (b) undo() must peek before it pops, not pop then check: var last = history[history.length - 1]; and only history.pop() once the branch has actually restored something. As written the move branch already destroys the entry when the item is missing, which is how pressing Undo after a delete silently empties the bar; the finding's 'do NOT pop' instruction cannot be honoured after the pop has run. (c) After restore, call place(measureEl) and focus the restored row's .b-grab (not a stepper, which no longer exists), matching the gate's 'undo returns focus to the control that made the change' intent. (d) Give paintUndo a kind branch before it computes Math.abs(top.to - top.from) - a delete entry has no to/from, so the existing line would print NaN; the delete text should read 'Last change: <title> deleted.' with no .num span, or with the count omitted. (e) For the focus-after-delete half, prefer focusing the .b-grab of the row that took the deleted row's place (last.nextNode) and falling back to the previous row, then to the section heading if the list is now empty - the finding stops at 'next or previous' and leaves the emptied-list case undefined.
